topic: Unveiling Euler's Identity: The Most Beautiful Equation
target_audience: High school students with basic trigonometry and complex number knowledge

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane
lecture_lines: Meet the complex plane: real and imaginary axes.
Think of complex numbers as vectors.
A point like 3+4i defines a position.
animations: Fade in the complex plane with labeled real/imaginary axes (#FFFFFF).
Plot a point z = x + iy on the complex plane (#00FF00).
Draw a vector from the origin to z (#FF0000).

sections.title: Rotational Motion and the Exponential Function
animations: Show a unit circle on the complex plane (#FFFFFF).
Animate a point moving along the circle counter-clockwise (#FFFF00).
Display the angle θ changing over time (#FF00FF).

sections.title: Euler’s Formula: Linking Circles and Exponentials
lecture_lines: Euler's formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ).
Angle θ sweeps an arc on the circle.
Tracing coordinates as cos and sin.
Input θ links circles to exponentials.
animations: Display the formula e^(iθ) = cosθ + isinθ in large font (#FFFFFF).
Highlight cosθ on the real axis and isinθ on imaginary (#FF0000, #00FF00).
Show the resulting point z = e^(iθ) on the unit circle (#FFFF00).
Animate the point z tracing the circle as θ changes.
Finalize with the full equation centered on screen.

sections.title: The Grand Finale: Deriving e^(πi) = -1
animations: Substitute θ = π into the formula (#FF00FF).
Highlight -1 on the real axis with a glow effect.

sections.title: Synthesis and Beauty
lecture_lines: Connecting five constants: e, i, π, 1, 0.
animations: Fade in the constants e, i, π, 1, 0 in separate colors.
Slowly zoom out to show the beautiful connection between these numbers.
